answer:
Yes, the handover can be modelled as a documentable event — but the informality is not what limits you, and the thing you cannot say is not the thing the question worries about.

1. Undated, unwitnessed and informal are not obstacles in the CRM. An event is an event whether or not anyone recorded it. E52 Time-Span's own scope note contemplates "An extreme case of approximation, might, for example, define an instance of E52 Time-Span having unknown beginning, end and duration", and says such a time-span "may, nevertheless, be associated with other descriptions by which people can infer knowledge about it, such as in relative chronologies". Concretely: give the handover an E52 Time-Span and bound it with P82 at some time within (outer bound only, no inner bound), and/or place it in the chain with the topological primitives (P182 ends before or with the start of, P183 ends before the start of, P175/P176), which order temporal entities with no dates at all. The reference model discusses this under 'Relations with Events > Temporal Relations' and 'Specific Modelling Constructs > Temporal Relation Primitives based on fuzzy boundaries'. Lack of witnesses is likewise irrelevant — P11 had participant and P12 occurred in the presence of are optional in practice (quantifiers are semantic, not implementation constraints).

2. The real gap is a property gap, not an epistemic one: the CRM has no way to say that an event transferred a right. `connect E7 E30` and `connect E8 E30` return only P16 used specific object, P17 was motivated by, P15 was influenced by and P12 — nothing directional, nothing that says who gave up and who received. E8 Acquisition looks like the answer and is not: its P24 transferred title of ranges over E18 Physical Thing, and the SIG's own added scope note (Issue 87, closed Copenhagen 2002) states that an E8 implies establishment or loss of ownership rights on physical objects but "does not, however, imply changes of rights in general". On crm-sig, Robert Sanderson wrote in t1019 that transfer of a Right cannot be modelled, and the construct that was designed to fix it — the CRMsoc class Right Holding, an n-ary relation carrying the time-span of a right being held (Issue 335) — was merged into Issue 408 at the 43rd meeting and finally closed when the SIG "resolved to discontinue work on CRMsoc" at the 60th meeting in April 2025 (Issues 172, 330, 335, 343, 421 all funnel into that outcome). So as of the current standard there is no ratified construct for the temporal history of right-holding, and P75 possesses is deliberately atemporal — its scope note reads "holds or has held a legal claim", which is exactly why it cannot carry a chain.

3. What to build instead. The pattern Stephen Stead put to the SIG in that same thread is the one available in CRMbase: give the right a temporal extent through an activity rather than through the right itself. For this case that works unusually well, because the tenure is not passive — the fire-keeper actually strikes the flame every midsummer, in public.
  - The right: one E30 Right, P2 has type an E55 Type such as 'customary prerogative', P75 possesses from each keeper. (See the caveat in 4.)
  - Each keeper's tenure: an E7 Activity, P2 has type 'fire-keeping', P14 carried out by the keeper with P14.1 in the role of 'fire-keeper', P16 used specific object the E30 Right, P4 has time-span an E52 bounded by the first and last lighting you have evidence for.
  - The chain the project wants: P134 continued between consecutive tenure activities. Its scope note is exactly this — "the domain is considered as an intentional continuation of the range", and "Continuation implies a coherence of intentions and outcomes". Because P134 is a subproperty of P176i it also carries the ordering, so the chain is asserted even where no date is.
  - The handover itself: a separate E7 Activity, P2 has type 'fire-keeper succession', P14 carried out by the outgoing keeper (the case says the moment is his alone to choose, so he is the agent), P11 had participant the successor, P16 used specific object the E30 Right, P4 has time-span an E52 with P82 at some time within giving outer bounds — in practice bracketed by the predecessor's last lighting and the successor's first — or left dateless and merely ordered with P182 against those two lightings. Document the fact of transfer as the succession of the two tenure activities plus this typed activity; do not expect a property to spell out 'transferred right to/from', because there is none.
  - The community coming to accept the new keeper over a year or two: this is not the handover and should not be collapsed into it. It is someone else's opinion about who holds the right, and E13 Attribute Assignment is built for registering exactly that: P14 carried out by the village community (an E39 Actor, in practice an E74 Group), P177 assigned property of type = P75 possesses, P140 assigned attribute to = the successor, P141 assigned = the E30 Right, P4 has time-span the fuzzy one-to-two-year window. Per 'Modelling principles > Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents' and the E13 scope note, using E13 marks the maintaining team as neutral to the assertion's validity while recording whose opinion it is and how it came about. A second E13 records the documentation project's own dated claim.
  - The project's inference that a handover happened at all: where nobody testified, CRMinf is the honest home for it — an I2 Belief held by the project, J4 that an I4 Proposition Set (that keeper A passed the right to keeper B within window W), J5 holds to be an I6 Belief Value short of certainty. Stephen Stead pointed the list at CRMinf for precisely the case where the truth of a right-holding statement is at issue.

4. Two things to be honest about. First, whether E30 Right fits at all. Its scope note says "legal privileges", and Martin Doerr told the list that the CRM "contains the notion of 'E30 Right' only to the degree normally documented in museums as pertaining to museum objects". A village custom with no legal instrument behind it sits at the edge of that. Using E30 with an explicit P2 has type is defensible and is what the CRM's minimality leaves you, but the project should record that it is stretching the class, not assume the model endorses it. If they prefer not to stretch it, the tenure-plus-P134 chain with P14.1 in the role of 'fire-keeper' carries almost all the documentary value without instantiating E30 at all. Second, 'unbroken' is the one claim to refuse. Under 'Modelling principles > Monotonicity' the CRM is an Open World model: the absence of a recorded handover is not evidence that no handover happened, so a graph of consecutive tenures linked by P134 records the continuity you have evidence for and cannot assert that the chain has no gaps. If the project wants 'unbroken' stated, that is a claim of theirs and belongs in an E13 or an I2 Belief attributed to them, not in the event layer.

So: in scope, with a named limit. Model the succession as a typed E7 Activity with a fuzzy or purely ordinal time-span; model the tenure chain with P134; put the community's acceptance and the project's own inference in E13 / CRMinf. Do not model it as a transfer of legal title, and do not expect the model to certify the chain as complete.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its P24 transferred title of ranges over E18 Physical Thing, and the scope-note sentence the SIG added under Issue 87 says an E8 'does not, however, imply changes of rights in general'. Nothing physical changes hands here and no legal title moves.

Scoped to transfers of physical custody, or legal responsibility for physical custody, of objects (P30 transferred custody of -> E18). The right to strike the first flame is not custody of the bonfire or of any object.

Would require inventing an E74 Group of 'the fire-keepers' so the successor could join it and the predecessor leave. There is no such body — the office has one holder and no organisation. Christian-Emil Smith Ore called this device 'The group trick ... introduced as an ad hock' and not good ontological practice in t1806.

It is the class this case wants — an n-ary relation carrying the time-span over which a specific actor holds specific rights over a legal object — but it was never ratified. Issue 335 was merged into Issue 408 at the 43rd meeting and Issue 408 closed at the 60th meeting (April 2025) when the SIG resolved to discontinue work on CRMsoc. Proposing it would be citing a withdrawn extension.

rejected_alternatives.option: E65 Creation / E63 Beginning of Existence and E64 End of Existence of a fresh E30 Right per keeper
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The workaround Sanderson described (create and destroy hierarchical Rights to avoid modelling a transfer). It fails on the CRM's own terms: E30 is an E28 Conceptual Object, whose existence ends only when the last carrier and the last memory are lost, so you cannot end the predecessor's right. That objection is what started t1019.

rejected_alternatives.option: CRMaaa ZE6 Social Status / SDHSS C13 Social Role Embodiment
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Named by George Bruseker and Francesco Beretta in t1806 as the extensions built for exactly this kind of held-role social fact, after Martin Doerr's 'CRMbase is minimal, deliberately' and Bruseker's 'CRMbase cannot express this in a straightforward way'. They are the right direction if the project can adopt an extension, but neither is retrievable through this search system (concept ZE6 and concept C13 both return 'No such concept'), so I will not put identifiers I could not inspect into the recommendation.

rejected_alternatives.option: P75 possesses alone, one triple per keeper
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The simplest thing the project might try, and it silently loses the chain. P75 is untemporal by design — 'holds or has held a legal claim' — so a set of P75 triples records the membership of the keeper list but neither the order nor the handovers, which is the whole deliverable. Issue 172 'Temporality of rights' was raised for this and ended unresolved with CRMsoc.

siblings_considered.why_not: The other subclass of E5 that could take the handover. E63 Beginning of Existence would assert that something persistent came into being at that moment — the successor's right. That is the reading the SIG rejected in t1019: a right qua conceptual object exists independently of the period over which it is valid, so the handover brings nothing into existence. E7 Activity is correct because the handover is an intentional act by an actor that changes a social state.

E73 Information Object is E30's only sibling under E89. Nothing in this case is an identifiable immaterial item with an objectively recognisable structure: the custom is unwritten, there is no text, formula or prescription. If the documentation project writes the custom's rules down, that written statement is an E73, but the prerogative itself is not one.

The nearest sibling under E7 and the one a reader would reach for, since 'succession' sounds like a transfer. Ruled out for the reason in rejected_alternatives: P24 transferred title of ranges over E18 Physical Thing and Issue 87's scope-note addition denies that E8 implies changes of rights in general. E13 is what I need instead, because what the community and the project actually produce is an assertion about who possesses the right, not a title transfer.

Both are siblings under E1 and E92 Spacetime Volume is the temptation for a phenomenon with fuzzy edges. But what is unknown here is when, not where; asserting a 4-dimensional extent for a private conversation between two people would add a spatial claim the sources do not support. E52 Time-Span, whose scope note explicitly allows unknown beginning, end and duration, is exactly the right degree of commitment.

concept I2 prints no siblings block — the tool does not compute siblings for CRMinf classes — so I cannot name a verified sibling. The closest rival I did weigh is E13 Attribute Assignment, and I use both: E13 records who asserted that a keeper possesses the right, while I2 Belief plus J5 holds to be lets the project attach a belief value short of certainty to the proposition that an unwitnessed handover occurred.

notes: The system was strong here. `connect E7 E30` and `connect E8 E30` returning no transfer-shaped property was the single most informative result — an empty answer that told me the gap is in the model, not in my search. The issue register then closed the question fast: 172 -> 421 -> 408 chained cleanly, and the 60th-meeting minutes confirmed CRMsoc was discontinued, which is what makes 'Right Holding' unusable rather than merely unfinished. Two frictions. (1) `docs` truncates each hit to roughly 250 characters, so I could establish that 'Modelling principles > Monotonicity' has a fourth consequence about time-dependent properties such as owner and location, but could not read the rest of the paragraph; I cited the section rather than paraphrase what I could not see. (2) Extension classes are partly opaque: `concept I2` gives full scope note and properties but prints no siblings block, and the CRMaaa/SDHSS classes named in t1806 (ZE6, C13) return 'No such concept', so I could name them as directions without being able to check them. Residual uncertainty in the answer, and the reason for medium rather than high, is not the mechanism but E30 Right's applicability: its scope note says 'legal privileges', Doerr's 2002 message confines it to what museums document about museum objects, and I found no later SIG statement broadening it to customary or non-legal prerogatives. Every thread `concept E30` lists for that question (t0972, t0983, t1019) is marked unresolved, which is itself the answer — the SIG never settled it.
